O R D E R

The second accused in C.C.No.110 of 1999 on the files of the Court of the Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Kottayam filed this Revision Petition challenging the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sections 16(1)(a)(i) read with Section 2(ia)(a)(j)(m), 7(i) and 17(1)(a)(b) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short 'the PFAAct').
2. Heard.
3.

entities.text:
Court of the Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Kottayam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:-
On 11.10.1995 at about 2.30 p.m., PW1, the Food Inspector, purchased 750 grams of peas dhall from the shop of the first accused.
Second accused was the owner of the said shop.
After taking samples as per rules, one of the samples was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst.

The Public Analyst filed Ext. P11 report stating that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for peas dhall under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1956 and therefore, the same was adulterated.
It was further stated that the sample contained synthetic colouring matter.
Thereafter, on the request of the accused, the second sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis.
Ext.P15 certificate of the Central Food Laboratory would show that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for food grains as per the PFA Rules and therefore, it was adulterated.
4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW3 were examined and Exts. P1 to P10 series were marked for the prosecution.
DW1 was examined for the revision petitioner.

5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext. P15 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated.
The learned counsel for the revision petitioner relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument.

entities.text: Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. In this case, Admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was prescribed as mandated under Section 23 (1-A)
(ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act.

Therefore, Ext. P15 certificate of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case was adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra).

It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal.

In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food M.K.Khadar vs Food Inspector on 8 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94711362/
2 Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) and found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and accordingly, the Court acquitted the accused.

Gopalakrishnan v. Food M.K.Khadar vs Food Inspector on 8 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94711362/

sentences.text: The matter was referred to a Division Bench and the Division Bench also affirmed the said decision, submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.

Even otherwise, in view of the decision of the Pepsico India Holdings (supra), the conviction in this case cannot be sustained as no laboratory was notified and no validated method of analysis was specified as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

In the result, this Revision Petition stands allowed setting aside the conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sections 16(1)(a)(i) read with Section 2(ia)(a)(j)(m), 7(i) and 17(1)(a)(b) of the PFA Act, 1954 and the revision petitioner is acquitted for the said offence.
The bail bond of the revision petitioner stands cancelled and he is set at liberty.
